'''Diamond Stone''' (born February 10, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]] in the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].

==High school career==
[[File:20150401 MCDAAG Diamond Stone dunk 3 (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Stone dunking in front of [[Stephen Zimmerman]] in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]]]]
Stone graduated from [[Dominican High School (Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin)|Dominican High School]] in [[Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin]]. As a senior he averaged 24.4 points and 11.7 rebounds per game. He finished his career with 2,193 points.<ref>[http://www.whitefishbaynow.com/sports/dominicans-diamond-stone-left-a-mark-that-will-be-remembered-for-decades-b99474580z1-299046571.html Dominican's Diamond Stone left a mark that will be remembered for decades]</ref> During his four years he helped lead Dominican to four-straight WIAA Division 4 state championships.<ref>[http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/badgers-men-s-basketball-uw-loses-out-to-maryland-in/article_c1a75fe4-4b6d-5956-903e-0c915b809da3.html Badgers men's basketball: UW loses out to Maryland in Diamond Stone sweepstakes]</ref>

During the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]], Stone hit 7 of 9 shots for 14 points and also had three rebounds.<ref>[http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/terrapins-insider/wp/2015/04/01/maryland-commit-diamond-stone-scores-14-points-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game/ Maryland commit Diamond Stone scores 14 points in McDonald’s All-American Game]</ref><ref>[http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bal-diamond-stone-impresses-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game-sparking-ncaa-title-talk-20150401-story.html Diamond Stone impresses in McDonald's All American Game, sparking NCAA title talk]</ref>

== College career ==
Stone was a five-star recruit.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/lsu/basketball/recruiting/player-Diamond-Stone-131549 Rivals.com bio]</ref><ref>[http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/5894071n-diamond-stone Scout.com bio]</ref><ref>[http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/145063/diamond-stone Espn.com bio]</ref> In March 2015 he committed to the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] to play [[college basketball]].<ref>[http://www.jsonline.com/sports/preps/diamond-stone-chooses-maryland-b99470549z1-297856071.html Diamond Stone chooses Maryland]</ref><ref>[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12573509/diamond-stone-no-7-espn-100-commits-maryland-terrapins Diamond Stone commits to Terps]</ref> He signed on April 15.<ref>[http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bal-diamond-stone-signs-with-maryland-20150415-story.html Diamond Stone signs agreement to join Terps]</ref> On December 30, 2015, Stone broke a Maryland freshman school record, scoring 39 points in a game against the [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Stone Scores 39, Leads #4 Terps Past Penn State|url = http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=210607587|website = umterps.com|accessdate = 2015-12-31}}</ref> On February 16, 2016, Stone was suspended by Coach Mark Turgeon for one game against Minnesota for hitting a Wisconsin player's head against the court and received a flagrant-1 foul.

==Professional career==
At the end of his only season at Maryland, Stone would be one of 59 college/postgraduate underclassmen to enter the [[2016 NBA Draft]]. Stone is projected to being either a late first round or early second round draft pick after starting out the season as an early lottery draft pick.
